methodological_rigor.justification: Single-center retrospective cohort with an as-treated approach is reasonable for descriptive practice-pattern reporting, but the comparative inferential aim (CT+IO vs CT alone) is undermined by a very small CT-alone arm (n=32 vs n=82) and multiple acknowledged baseline imbalances (sex, histology, ECOG, brain metastases, platinum backbone) that are only partially addressed in a Cox model limited to variables with univariate p<0.1. No a priori power calculation is reported, which the authors concede caused likely underpowering. No propensity score matching, IPTW, or formal confounder adjustment beyond a sparse multivariate model was performed. Missing-data handling for the 24.4% missing ECOG PS is limited to a sensitivity analysis. Progression ascertainment was not RECIST-standardized (Section 4), introducing information bias, and no multiplicity correction is applied to the several subgroup/sensitivity comparisons.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Design is an individual retrospective cohort study at one academic center, mapping to Oxford LoE 2b. The clinical question (real-world effectiveness and tolerability of CT+IO in PD-L1<1% advanced NSCLC) is clinically important and uses patient-relevant endpoints (rwOS, rwPFS, clinically significant TRAEs/irAEs). However, the study yields null primary comparisons with wide confidence intervals that cannot change practice and largely confirms the trial-to-real-world gap already described by Verschueren, Wallrabenstein, and Liu/Velcheti (refs 11-14). The most actionable observations (documentation gaps, patient refusal rate, decision-aid uptake) are hypothesis-generating rather than practice-altering.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE is the applicable checklist for this retrospective observational cohort. Key items are present: eligibility and setting (Section 2.1), variable definitions, outcome definitions (Section 2.3), flow of participants (Figure 1 referenced), descriptive tables, and a thoughtful limitations section covering selection, information, and confounding biases. However, several STROBE items are weak or absent: there is no sample size justification, no explicit statement of how continuous variables were handled, missingness per variable is not systematically tabulated, and sensitivity-analysis results are summarized only partially. The blinded manuscript contains no data-availability or code-availability statement, no repository identifiers, and no analytic code reference, so reproducibility is minimal.

novelty_literature.justification: The work is empirically incremental: it adds a Canadian single-center real-world cohort to a growing set of similar studies in PD-L1<1% advanced NSCLC treated with CT+IO (Wallrabenstein 2023, Verschueren 2024, Liu 2022, Velcheti 2021; refs 11-14 in the manuscript itself). No new mechanism, methodology, biomarker, or trial design is introduced, and the central finding (null comparison attributed to underpowering plus a trial-to-real-world gap) replicates established observations. Mild novelty lies in the practice-pattern descriptors (reasons for not choosing CT+IO, patient refusal rate, ECOG documentation gaps) and the squamous subgroup receiving second-line nivolumab, though the latter is explicitly exploratory and underpowered.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written and well organized, with a logical introduction, structured methods, and a discussion that candidly engages with the study's limitations (baseline imbalances, non-RECIST progression ascertainment, missing ECOG, selection bias). Acronyms (NSCLC, PD-L1, CT, IO, OS, PFS, irAE, TRAE) are expanded on first use, and comparisons to KN189/KN407/CM9LA are quantitatively framed. The abstract is unusually structured as two paragraphs (a lay summary followed by a structured abstract), which is somewhat redundant, and some discussion passages (e.g., on imaging interval heterogeneity) could be tightened. Table and figure callouts are appropriate even though the visuals are not available for inspection.

key_strengths: Clinically relevant real-world question in an understudied PD-L1<1% advanced NSCLC population
Candid, well-structured discussion of baseline imbalances, selection/information bias, and underpowering
Toxicity and irAE reporting benchmarked quantitatively against KN189 and KN407
Captures practice-pattern insights (reasons for not choosing CT+IO, patient refusal, ECOG documentation gaps) not available from trials
Sensitivity analysis for missing ECOG PS and exploratory histology subgroup analyses pre-declared as such
key_concerns: Small CT-alone comparator (n=32) with multiple unaddressed baseline imbalances and no propensity score / IPTW adjustment
No a priori power calculation; null primary findings are of uncertain inferential value
Non-RECIST progression ascertainment and heterogeneous imaging intervals introduce information bias in rwPFS
24.4% missing ECOG PS handled only via a single sensitivity analysis; variable-level missingness not tabulated
Findings are largely confirmatory of prior real-world cohorts (Wallrabenstein, Verschueren, Liu, Velcheti) with limited incremental novelty
No data-availability or code-sharing statement in the blinded manuscript
chief_reviewer.rationale: A competently reported but small, single-center, confirmatory real-world cohort with null primary comparisons and acknowledged confounding; appropriate for a lower-tier oncology journal with minor revisions to clarify missing-data handling, confounder adjustment, and data availability.
